## Submission 1b: Data Cleaning

```{r}

#clean maternal vitamin D measurements
#the original values have text before the measurement
#so remove everything before the colon, then convert the values
#to numeric, so vitamin D concentrations can be continuous.
covarData <- covarData |>  
  mutate(mat_vitD = as.numeric(str_remove(mat_vitD, ".*:"))
         )

#confirm that vitamin D is numeric
#class(covarData$mat_vitD)
#summarize the data to check if everything is reasonable
#summary(covarData$mat_vitD)

#create a categorical vitamin D variable from the continuous
#measurement so that individuals with levels < 30ng/ml are
#insufficient and >= 30ng/ml are sufficient
covarData <- covarData |>  
  mutate( 
    vitData = if_else(mat_vitD >= 30, "Sufficient", "Insufficient")
  ) 

#count the individuals in each vitamin D group
#table(covarData$vitData)

#rename first column of the gene expression set
#contains microarray probe IDs but imported as "X" so renaming
#it to match it to the gene names set.
geneexpressionData <- geneexpressionData |>  
  rename(PROBEID = X)

#turn the gene expression data to long format
#long format puts all sample IDs into one column and 
#expression values in another so each row can represent 1
#probe measurement for 1 sample. 
#PROBEID column unchanged, need to match with the genes
geneexpressionLong <- geneexpressionData |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -PROBEID, 
    names_to = "geoID", 
    values_to = "expression"
  )

#check to see if the gene names set has duplicate probe IDs
#which could make more rows when merging sets
#sum(duplicated(genenamesData$PROBEID))

#look at the original pregnancy outcome categories
#to see how normal pregnancy and preeclampsia are recorded
#table(covarData$preg_preeclampsia)

#clean the pregnancy outcome labels
#remove "pregnancy_condition:"
#makes it much simpler for boxplot
covarData <- covarData |>  
  mutate(preg_preeclampsia = str_remove(preg_preeclampsia,
                                        "pregnancy_condition: "))
#confirm that everything is correct and
#count individuals for normal / preeclampsia
#table(covarData$preg_preeclampsia)

#merge all three data sets
#match gene expression measurements to gene names
#using PROBEID, then match those to maternal
#characteristics using geoID, then it should 
#result in a data set that gives you gene expression
#+ gene name + participant info all together
mergeData <- geneexpressionLong |>  
  left_join(genenamesData, by = "PROBEID") |>  
  left_join(covarData, by = "geoID")

#look at merged data and check dimensions / 
#first few rows
#dim(mergeData)
#head(mergeData)

```

## Submission 1c: Gene Selection

```{r}

#select SGK1 gene, it's involved in cellular
#response to hormonal signals and stress
#filtering keeps only the expression associated with it
geneData <- mergeData |>  
  filter(GENE == "SGK1")
```

## Submission 1d: Visualization

```{r}
#plot 1: histogram of SGK1 gene expression
#describes how SGK1 expression is distributed across the 
#sample, with the x axis showing expression values and the y
#showing participant n.
#looking at most common expression values / overall shape 
ggplot(geneData, aes(x = expression)) + 
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.1, 
    fill = "#377EB8",
    color = "black"
  ) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(7.4, 9.0, by = 0.2)
  ) + 
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 10), 
    limits = c(0, 40),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) + 
  labs( 
    title = " ", 
    x = "SGK1 Gene Expression",
    y = "Number of Participants"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "gray40",
      fill = NA, 
      linewidth = 0.5
    ), 
    plot.title = element_text( 
      hjust = 0,
      face = "plain"
      ),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10)
    )

```


```{r}

#plot 2: scatterplot of maternal vitamin D and SGK1 expression
#describes the relationship between vitamin D concentration and
#gene expression, with both variables being continuous. 
#each point is one individual's vitamin D concentration and
#SGK1 expression.
ggplot(geneData, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression)) + 
  geom_point(
    color = "#377EB8",
    size = 2, 
    alpha = 0.7
  ) + 
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(7.4, 9.0, by = 0.2)
  ) + 
  labs( 
    title = " ",  
    x = "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)",
    y = "SGK1 Gene Expression"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "gray40",
      fill = NA, 
      linewidth = 0.5
    ), 
    plot.title = element_text( 
      hjust = 0,
      face = "plain"
      ),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10)
    )

```


```{r}

#plot3: boxplot of SGK1 expression by pregnancy outcome and vitamin D status. 
#compares gene expression across two categorical variables
#pregnancy outcome places individuals into normal and
#preeclampsia groups. Vitamin D status places individuals
#into sufficient and insufficient groups. 
#each box summarizes the distribution of SGK1 expression
#within one group.
ggplot(geneData, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = expression, fill = vitData)) + 
  geom_boxplot(
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.8
  ) + 
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Insufficient" = "#377EB8",
               "Sufficient" = "#E15759")
  ) + 
  labs( 
    x = NULL,
    y = "SGK1 Gene Expression", 
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_rect(
      color = "gray40",
      fill = NA, 
      linewidth = 0.5
    ), 
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"),
    plot.title = element_text( 
      hjust = 0,
      face = "plain"
      )
  )

```
